title: Phased commit flow with operator escrow for Optimize recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a sentinelized, phased commit flow for automatic Optimize suggestions (batching and KV-cache recommendations) that requires operator escrow for final activation. The goal is to allow low-risk automated application of cost-saving configs while guaranteeing human-in-the-loop control for higher-risk changes. The flow combines simulated canaries, metrics-driven gating, and an operator escrow window where an on-call engineer can review telemetry before final rollout. Deliverables: 1) a policy engine extension that classifies suggestions by risk and selects an appropriate apply pipeline; 2) a canary simulation harness to run prospective changes against sampled traffic and synthetic loads; 3) an escrow UI in Console for operator approval/timeout and manual rollback; 4) automated rollback recipes and an observable audit trail (PR, change event, telemetry snapshot). Links: Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Phased+Commit+with+Operator+Escrow, Design spec: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1OptFlowDraft, Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1824
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can tag suggestions as low/medium/high risk and route to the correct pipeline
Simulation canary run produces pass/fail and a standardized telemetry artifact stored in S3/obs
Operator escrow UI shows telemetry snapshot, proposed config diff, and a single-click approve/reject with timestamped audit
Automated apply performs staged activation: soft-apply to 2% traffic, monitor 15m, expand to 20%, monitor 1h, full apply at 24h if gates pass
Rollback executes automatically on gate failure and surfaces root-cause metrics in the Console incident view
End-to-end e2e test that runs a simulated suggestion through policy -> canary -> escrow -> staged apply and verifies observability hooks
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind opt-in tenant list; infra-only rollout to test cluster
Phase 1: Internal dogfood tenants; run dry-run mode (no real writes) to validate telemetry and artifacts
Phase 2: Canary enabled with synthetic traffic; verify gating thresholds and rollback playbook
Phase 3: Operator escrow enforced for high/medium risk recommendations; low-risk can bypass escrow for soft apply
Phase 4: Gradual increase of autoapply percentage and expansion to customers with explicit opt-in
Phase 5: Post-launch review and automated tuning to threshold heuristics based on observed false-positive/negative rates

qa_notes: Prepare synthetic traffic scenarios for large sequence lengths to test KV cache behavior.
Run long-tail latency sweeps during canary expansion windows to detect regressions in percentiles > p95.
Validate that rollback resets only the changed config keys and does not interfere with user-pinned versions.
risks: False positives in canary simulation could block beneficial cost savings if thresholds are too strict.
Escrow delays may increase time-to-value for customers if operator bandwidth is limited; need escalation SLA.
Inadequate observability could make root-cause analysis slow after a rollback, increasing customer impact.
